players.product: regulated electric service, gas generation and transmission build for hyperscale data centers in the Gulf South (Meta Richland Parish LA, Amazon Mississippi)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 results: CEO reported '2025 adjusted earnings per share of $3.91, which is in the top half of our guidance range' and said Entergy continues to expect 'greater than 8% adjusted EPS annual growth through 2029'; 2025 had 4% sales growth driven by a 7% increase in industrial sales (CFO: excluding weather, retail sales rose approximately 4%, with industrial the largest contributor including new and expansion projects ramping up).
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted earnings per share of $3.91; 4% sales growth; 7% increase in industrial sales; greater than 8% adjusted EPS annual growth through 2029

quarterly_data.signal: Sales outlook (point-in-time): off 2025 weather-adjusted results Entergy expects 'an expected 8% compound annual growth rate through 2029 from 2025 and driven by 15% industrial growth'; CFO said data centers are the primary driver, alongside LNG, primary metals, industrial gases, petrochemicals and agricultural chemicals, and hyperscale data centers enter the plan only once an ESA is in place and only at minimum build levels.
quarterly_data.figure: 8% compound annual growth rate through 2029; 15% industrial growth

quarterly_data.signal: Large-load contracting: 'Last year, we signed electric service agreements totaling approximately 3.5 gigawatts', with new data center announcements in Arkansas, Louisiana and Mississippi 'including both colocation developers and hyperscalers'; the pipeline is 'unchanged at 7 to 12 gigawatts for data centers and 3 to 5 gigawatts for other industries'. Asked about political and regulatory feedback, the CEO said the positive momentum 'continues to bode well for the expectations that we've laid out for you all. In fact, I think they probably strengthened since we talked to you last quite a bit'.
quarterly_data.figure: signed electric service agreements totaling approximately 3.5 gigawatts; 7 to 12 gigawatts for data centers and 3 to 5 gigawatts for other industries

quarterly_data.signal: Generation equipment secured: CEO said Entergy has 'clear line of sight on equipment to serve 8 gigawatts of incremental load above our current plan' and has confirmed EPC engagement for projects in and beyond its outlooks; CFO said there is 'about 8 gigawatts of turbines and other plant island equipment available for growth' not yet tied to specific ESAs, and the Cottonwood addition does not replace any of those turbines. CEO: Entergy fully expects to use the ordered turbines on their ordered time line ('We have customers that would move them forward if they could'); if ESAs are not in place when turbine payments start, it would likely get reimbursement agreements from customers.
quarterly_data.figure: about 8 gigawatts of turbines and other plant island equipment available for growth

quarterly_data.signal: Capital plan (point-in-time): the customer-centric capital plan is now $43 billion through 2029, $2 billion higher than the preliminary plan shown at EEI, with the increase largely the Cottonwood Generating Station plus some 2025 capital rolled into 2026; the 2026 capital plan is $11.6 billion, approximately $3.6 billion higher than 2025; in 2025 Entergy invested $8 billion, about half of it in generation.
quarterly_data.figure: $43 billion capital plan through 2029; $2 billion higher than our preliminary plan; For 2026, our capital plan is $11.6 billion; In 2025, we invested $8 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Generation build: nearly 9 GW of gas, solar and battery storage approved and under construction toward 13 GW of new capacity over the next 4 years; Orange County Advanced Power Station is in final stages ahead of a summer in-service date; early-stage projects include Franklin Farms Units 1 and 2 and Waterford 5 (Louisiana), Legend and Lone Star (Texas), Ironwood (Arkansas), Vicksburg Advanced Power Station and Trace View (Mississippi); 5 solar resources totaling 740 MW; Entergy Louisiana filed to acquire the Cottonwood facility for an upfront $1.5 billion plus $300 million of maintenance and improvement investment (decision requested by year-end); Waterford 6 and Westlake combined cycles were filed the day before the call. Nuclear fleet ran at a 90% unit capability factor, and Waterford 3 has a 45-megawatt upgrade planned later in the year.
quarterly_data.figure: nearly 9 gigawatts approved and under construction towards our planned 13 gigawatts of new capacity; 5 owned and contracted solar resources approved or in progress totaling 740 megawatts; upfront purchase price of $1.5 billion as well as $300 million of investment

quarterly_data.signal: Transmission and grid: Entergy invested about $3.5 billion in energy delivery in 2025, which includes accelerated resilience projects, and has invested $800 million in approved accelerated resilience work so far; the 4-year $17 billion customer-led energy delivery capital plan includes new construction on more than 570 miles of 500 kV lines and 175 miles of other transmission lines plus new substations, and $1.4 billion of approved projects to harden more than 45,000 assets; the Babel to Webre 500 kV project awaits a commission decision in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: We invested about $3.5 billion in 2025; 4-year $17 billion customer-led energy delivery capital plan; more than 570 miles of 500 kV lines; 175 miles of other transmission lines

quarterly_data.signal: Data-center contract economics (point-in-time): the data center contracts in place 'will generate approximately $5 billion in rate offsets' from their share of fixed costs over the contract lives, 'more than $5 per residential customer per month on average'; long-term data center contracts include early termination penalties and minimum bills, the forecast includes only the minimum bill, and the obligations are backstopped by the customers' parents.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $5 billion in rate offsets; more than $5 per residential customer per month

quarterly_data.signal: Funding the build (point-in-time): equity tied to the 4-year plan is unchanged at $4.4 billion, at the low end of the 10% to 15% of capital target, with $1 billion of hybrids in the back half of the forecast; about 45% of the 2026-2029 equity need is already contracted, so no new transaction is needed until well into 2027; in February Entergy settled an additional $345 million, about 4.6 million shares; 2026 nuclear PTC monetization is expected to net approximately $215 million.
quarterly_data.figure: equity associated with our 4-year plan is unchanged at $4.4 billion; about 45% is already contracted; $1 billion of hybrids; settled an additional $345 million or about 4.6 million shares

quarterly_data.signal: Regulatory and catalysts: in December the Louisiana PSC adopted the Louisiana Lightning Initiative, which lets utilities meet large new loads with RFP exemptions and expedited review (Arkansas and Mississippi have adopted similar rules); pending 2026 decisions include Arkansas Cypress Solar with battery storage, Babel to Webre 500 kV, and the Waterford 6 and Westlake combined cycles; Entergy Arkansas will file its first base rate case since 2015; Entergy will host an Investor Day on June 9 in New York City with 5-year outlooks. CEO said data-center support in its jurisdictions stays strong, with some concern about affordability and rates.

connects_to.relationship: regulated electric service and dedicated generation for Meta's Richland Parish, Louisiana hyperscale data center (full-tariff customer)

contracts.signal: Asked about Meta's lease terms with Blue Owl, CFO said to think of it as 2 separate transactions: on the electric service agreement 'we have a 15-year term with a subsidiary of Meta backstopped all the way at the parent', carrying termination fees and minimum bills, while Meta's transaction with Blue Owl is 'separate and apart from the ESA'. Asked who the ultimate guarantor is: 'It is the parent. It is Meta all the way up.'

connects_to.relationship: electric service for Hut 8's data center load (large-load colocator customer)

contracts.signal: Asked about Hut 8's announcement as the latest large-load ramp, CFO said 'I would think about Hut 8 and similarly sized data centers like we think about our probability weighted industrial growth overall', so it was already in the probability weighting rather than a discrete item like a hyperscaler. CEO said the first part of what Hut 8 announced 'doesn't add to the capital plan', but 'additional incremental growth in that customer would likely require incremental capital for capacity'. CFO said large-load customers, 'including not just the hyperscalers, but also colocators like a Hut 8', carry termination fees and minimum bills backstopped by their parents.
